$note: Acceptance-rule test vectors for guardian social recovery / key rotation. See README.md. A conforming verifier MUST reach the stated `accept` verdict for every case. Reference implementation of the rule: acceptance.py.
license_note: Public domain. Copy verbatim into any implementation; ship with a NIP. Full text: vectors/LICENSE.
generated_with: nostr-tools 2.23.9 / @noble/curves 2.0.1. Every event verifies as a Nostr event (cross-checked with nostr-sdk 0.44.2); the acceptance verdicts are cross-checked by acceptance.py, an independent Python implementation of the rule.
prev_sig_definition: BIP-340 Schnorr signature by the OLD key over the 32 raw bytes of the NEW x-only pubkey.
acceptance_rule: 1. a valid Guardian Set (kind 30101) signed by `old` exists, with threshold M and guardian set G
2. >= M distinct members of G published valid kind 30102 events with d == old and an identical `new`
3. each counted endorsement is signed by that guardian own key (pubkey in G)
4. a kind 30103 Rotation Claim signed by `new` exists with d == old; OR the claim carries a valid `prev-sig` (self-authorized, guardians not required)
5. the Guardian Set relied on is the most recent one whose created_at <= claim.created_at AND created_at + cooldown_seconds <= claim.created_at

cases.name: happy-path-threshold-met
cases.about: guardian set (thr 2) old enough; claim by NEW; 2 distinct guardians endorse NEW

cases.name: threshold-exceeded
cases.about: threshold 2, three guardians endorse — a minimum, not an exact count

cases.name: self-authorized-prev-sig
cases.about: planned rotation: claim carries a valid prev-sig by OLD over NEW; no guardians needed

cases.name: self-authorized-overrides-missing-threshold
cases.about: valid prev-sig short-circuits the guardian path even though only 1 of 2 guardians endorsed

cases.name: unrelated-events-ignored
cases.about: a happy path with extra noise — a kind-1 note and an attestation from a non-guardian — still accepts

cases.name: no-guardian-set
cases.about: claim + 2 endorsements but no kind 30101 anywhere

cases.name: guardian-set-not-signed-by-old
cases.about: the kind 30101 is signed by G4, not by OLD — it does not bind OLD

cases.name: threshold-not-met
cases.about: guardian set threshold 3; only 2 guardians endorse

cases.name: mismatched-new-keys
cases.about: two guardians endorse, but for different successor keys — no single new key reaches threshold

cases.name: duplicate-guardian
cases.about: the same guardian (G1) publishes two endorsements to fake reaching threshold 2

cases.name: endorser-not-a-guardian
cases.about: guardian set is {G1,G2} thr 2; G1 endorses and G4 endorses, but G4 is not a guardian

cases.name: no-rotation-claim
cases.about: guardian set + 2 endorsements but no kind 30103 claim

cases.name: claim-signed-by-old-key
cases.about: the claim is signed by OLD, so it names OLD as its own successor; the endorsements are for NEW

cases.name: guardian-set-inside-cooldown
cases.about: guardian set published only 2 days before the claim — inside the 7-day cool-down

cases.name: compromised-key-self-approval
cases.about: attacker holds OLD: installs a fresh guardian set of attacker keys and self-approves within the cool-down

cases.name: superseded-guardian-set
cases.about: an old thr-1 set and a newer thr-3 set are both eligible; the newer one governs and only 1 guardian endorsed

cases.name: guardian-set-after-claim
cases.about: the only guardian set was published after the claim — not in effect at the claim time

cases.name: prev-sig-over-wrong-key
cases.about: prev-sig is OLD signing MAL, not NEW — ignored; guardian path then has only 1 of 2

cases.name: prev-sig-by-non-old
cases.about: prev-sig is a valid BIP-340 signature over NEW but by G1, not OLD — ignored; guardian path has only 1 of 2
